summary: Instagram is doing nearly all the work: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly stay under 100 views. The best videos are about a single surprising idea ('the robot/sensor doesn't see, it only hears or feels') or a robot gimmick, and they get the most likes, saves and shares. Longer, generic 'how does X work?' questions about public places (taps, doors, lifts, smoke alarms) and the one English video are weak.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about a hands-on maker subject (robot, clap switch, PIR/IR sensor, mic) with a contrarian 'it doesn't do X, it only does Y' or 'without this, the robot falls' hook. Titles are short, punchy, 1-2 emojis, and the idea is a single surprising fact. Published recently, in tight bursts. Robot and clap-switch topics also earn the most shares and saves.
doMore: Lead with a contrarian 'doesn't see/hear, only does Y' hook on a robot or sensor topic
Make follow-ups to winners: gyro/balancing robot, clap switch, PIR, IR obstacle robot, mic
Post Instagram-first and test a Reel-native cut, since YouTube barely distributes these
Add a save/share trigger at the end, like 'save this for your next Arduino project'
Keep the Hindi title short with one emoji and a single clear surprise
stopDoing: Generic 'X Kaise Pehchanta Hai?' titles about public-place devices (taps, doors, lifts, malls)
Posting near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector, two IR-in-dark, two clap switch angles on the same week) that split views
English-only uploads while the audience is responding to Hindi
